description.en: AgentFairBench evaluates demographic disparity in the actions of LLM agents across hiring, lending, and medical triage. It uses synthetic, demographic-neutral profiles in counterfactual matched sets varying name-coded race/gender. Metrics include counterfactual flip rate, mean absolute score difference, action-rate disparity, and tool-invocation disparity, with bootstrap confidence intervals and FDR control.

evidence.snippet: We introduce AgentFairBench, a cheap, reproducible, multi-domain benchmark for demographic disparity in the actions of LLM agents.

claire_radar.motivation: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly take actions (screening applicants, recommending credit, triaging patients), yet fairness for LLMs is still measured by grading answers.

source.title: AgentFairBench: Do LLM Agents Discriminate When They Act?

claire_radar.whyItMatters: Existing fairness evaluations grade answers, not actions. AgentFairBench addresses the gap by measuring disparity in consequential agent decisions. Its low cost and reproducible harness provide a practical path for screening models for action-level bias before deployment.
